description: UMAP on 50,000 synthetic scRNA-seq cells — extreme CPU bubble, targets 85-90%+ GPU idle
prompt:
Perform UMAP dimensionality reduction on a very large synthetic single-cell RNA-seq dataset. Do everything in one code block.

1. Generate a count matrix: 50000 cells × 3000 genes. numpy.random.seed(42). Draw counts from numpy.random.negative_binomial(n=5, p=0.5, size=(50000, 3000)). Multiply each gene column by numpy.random.lognormal(mean=1.0, sigma=1.5, size=3000) to add per-gene baseline.
2. Normalize each cell to 10000 total counts (divide each row by its row sum, multiply by 10000), then apply numpy.log1p.
3. Select the top 500 genes by variance.
4. Run PCA to 30 components: sklearn.decomposition.PCA(n_components=30, random_state=42).
5. Run UMAP: import umap; reducer = umap.UMAP(n_components=2, n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, random_state=42); embedding = reducer.fit_transform(pca_result). This step will take 30-90 minutes — that is expected and normal for 50k cells on CPU.
6. Run KMeans with 12 clusters on the 2D embedding: sklearn.cluster.KMeans(n_clusters=12, random_state=42, n_init=10).
7. Print cluster sizes as a sorted table (cluster_id, n_cells, pct_of_total).

Do not generate any plots. Do not abort early. Report only the cluster sizes table.
notes: EXTREME bubble task. UMAP on 50k cells with umap-learn (pure CPU, pynndescent + numba JIT) takes 30-90 minutes. GPU is completely idle for the entire UMAP step. Expected GPU bubble: 85-92%. Timeout is 2 hours. This is the upper end of our bubble range.
